title: Minimum Flips in Binary Tree to Get Result
summary: Given a binary tree with leaf nodes representing boolean values and non-leaf nodes representing boolean operations, determine the minimum number of flips required to achieve a specified boolean result at the root.
statement: Given a binary tree with leaf nodes representing boolean values and non-leaf nodes representing boolean operations, determine the minimum number of flips required to achieve a specified boolean result at the root. Flips change leaf node values from true to false or vice versa. The evaluation of nodes follows their boolean operation on their children's evaluations. Each operation can only flip a leaf node. Always a solution exists, and NOT nodes have one child while other non-leaf nodes have two.
constraints: Leaves contain zero or one; internal nodes use 2=OR, 3=AND, 4=XOR, and unary 5=NOT.
One operation flips one leaf value.
Return the minimum flips needed for the root to evaluate to result.
